output_json.patch_notes: In extractFromJAR, after computing the target file splash = new File(splash, jarEntry), the code captures the intended cache directory (cacheDir) and compares canonical paths. If the target's canonical path does not start with the canonical cache directory path plus File.separator, extraction is refused and null is returned (matching the method's existing failure contract). The trailing separator prevents sibling-prefix bypasses. IOExceptions during canonicalization are logged and treated as failures. This blocks traversal while preserving normal in-directory extraction.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The guard only rejects entries resolving outside the cache directory; legitimate splash/library entries resolve inside it and are unaffected. Canonical path resolution follows symlinks (desired stricter containment). The method already returns null on failure paths, so callers handle null. Only compileJava was exercised; no unit test was added because the method is private and depends on process-wide launcher system properties, making an isolated regression test impractical without refactoring.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path-traversal (CWE-022) in extractFromJAR in Main.java. A malicious jar/zip entry name was used directly to build the output File and written via Files.copy, allowing writes outside the intended cache directory. Added a canonical-path containment check that refuses to extract entries resolving outside the cache directory.
